What is an air–sea or sea–air shipment?
How much cheaper and faster is it?

It is usually much cheaper than flying the whole way and much faster than shipping the whole way. The exact saving depends on the lane, so we show you the all-sea, all-air and bridge options side by side before you decide.
Which countries is it good for?

Landlocked countries reached through their capital airport, such as Afghanistan, Central Asia, Nepal, Uganda, Rwanda, Zambia, Malawi or Paraguay, and destinations with slow or infrequent sailings from India.
What cargo suits an air–sea bridge?

Goods that are too urgent or valuable for an all-sea transit but too heavy or bulky to justify all-air: spare parts, garments, electronics, machinery components and project parts that fit on aircraft pallets.
Do you handle the customs side?
Yes. We clear the export in India under our own customs broker licence, manage the transhipment documents at the hub, and coordinate import clearance at destination with our partners.

An international customs document, often called a passport for goods, that lets exhibition goods, commercial samples and professional equipment enter a country temporarily without paying duty. In India, carnets are issued and guaranteed by FICCI.
What if I don’t have a carnet?
Exhibition goods can usually still be imported temporarily without duty against a bond and an undertaking to re-export them within the allowed period. We handle the bond and the paperwork.
What happens if I sell exhibits at the show?
Goods sold or given away in India become a regular import. We clear them with the applicable duty paid and re-export the rest.
Can you deliver straight to the hall?
Yes. We coordinate with the venue and organiser’s official contractor so your crates reach the stand during build-up, and we collect them after the show.
How early should I contact you?
Ideally six to eight weeks before the show for sea freight, and three to four weeks for air. Last-minute shipments are possible, but cost more.

What is an air–sea or sea–air shipment?
A single shipment that uses both modes: part of the distance by ocean and the rest by air. Sea–air (sea first) is the most common; air–sea is used when the first leg is the urgent one.
How much cheaper and faster is it?

It is usually much cheaper than flying the whole way and much faster than shipping the whole way. The exact saving depends on the lane, so we show you the all-sea, all-air and bridge options side by side before you decide.
Which countries is it good for?

Landlocked countries reached through their capital airport, such as Afghanistan, Central Asia, Nepal, Uganda, Rwanda, Zambia, Malawi or Paraguay, and destinations with slow or infrequent sailings from India.
What cargo suits an air–sea bridge?

Goods that are too urgent or valuable for an all-sea transit but too heavy or bulky to justify all-air: spare parts, garments, electronics, machinery components and project parts that fit on aircraft pallets.
Do you handle the customs side?
Yes. We clear the export in India under our own customs broker licence, manage the transhipment documents at the hub, and coordinate import clearance at destination with our partners.

What is the difference between Advance Authorisation and EPCG?
Advance Authorisation lets you import inputs used to make export goods without duty. EPCG lets you import capital goods, such as machinery, at zero duty against a future export obligation.
Do I need BIS certification to import electronics?
Many electronic and IT products need BIS registration before they can be imported and sold in India. We check your product's status before you place the order.
